FILE:website/docs/start/glossary.md
4:description: The words this architecture uses precisely — including the two that are deliberately not synonyms.
7:# Glossary
9:This page exists because two words in this architecture are routinely used as
10:synonyms elsewhere and are **deliberately not** synonyms here: *domain* and
11:*feature*. Getting those two right explains why `core/domain` is singular while
12:`features/` is plural, and why one business subdomain can have three islands over
13:it. The rest of the page is the same treatment for every other term the docs use
17:The normative wording is
20:## Structure and layers
22:| Term | Meaning |
23:|---|---|
24:| **Domain (business subdomain)** | A business subdomain of the product — "tasks", "billing". Its frontend incarnation is a feature; one subdomain may have **several** islands (a list and a board over the same tasks are two islands over one subdomain). |
25:| **`core/domain`** | The shared language layer: entities, zod schemas, domain rules, the error taxonomy. Pure, isomorphic, and there is exactly **one** — it is the "domain" of hexagonal / ports-and-adapters, the vocabulary every vertical slice speaks. Depends on `zod` and nothing else. |
26:| **`core/contract`** | The API description shared by server and every client: routes with their methods and paths, I/O zod schemas, the response envelope. The **only** bridge between server and clients. |
27:| **`core/server`** | Use-cases plus the port interfaces they depend on. Framework-free. |
28:| **`core/client`** | The typed HTTP client and the query/mutation descriptor factories. Framework-free — it knows `@tanstack/query-core`, never React. |
29:| **Port** | A plain TypeScript `interface` in `core/server` (or `core/client`, for `AuthClientPort`) that names a capability the core needs. No decorators, no container. |
30:| **Adapter** | An implementation of a port, in `adapters/*`. Points *inward*: it imports the port, never the reverse. |
31:| **Composition root** | `apps/server/src/composition.ts` — the one place env decides which adapters run. Two sanctioned exceptions: the auth *client* adapter (bound in `apps/web/src/api.ts` and the CLI context) and `adapters/db/migrate.ts`. |
32:| **Platform entry** | `api/index.ts` — the Vercel serverless entry, allowed to import `apps/server` and nothing else. Where vendor env names such as `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` are mapped to neutral ones. |
33:| **Vocabulary library** | A dependency that is practically a language extension and would be a rewrite to swap: `zod`, `@tanstack/query-core`, the `@opentelemetry/api` no-op facade. Imported directly, on a per-layer allow-list. |
34:| **Infrastructure** | Anything with a plausible second implementation or a platform difference — frameworks, servers, drivers, providers. Lives behind a port, never in core. |
35:| **Port theater** | Wrapping a vocabulary library in an interface that will only ever have one implementation. Named examples deliberately *not* built: a `QueryPort` over TanStack Query, an `IStore` over the island-store library, a Sentry port. |
40:## Client state
42:| Term | Meaning |
43:|---|---|
44:| **Feature** | `apps/web/src/features/<name>/` — the vertical slice of a subdomain in the UI. |
45:| **Island** | The same feature, seen from its isolation guarantee: lint forbids features to import each other. One word names the thing, the other names its property — "feature (island)". |
46:| **View** | A React component inside a feature; renders UI and talks exclusively to its **own** island's core. |
47:| **Island core** | `features/<name>/core/` — a pure TS module: events in, selectors out, machine inside. A factory over its dependencies, DOM-free, node-runnable. |
48:| **Seam** | The island core's public API: `send(event)` in, `subscribe(listener)` for change notification, selectors out. Identical on every rung. |
49:| **Machine** | The state implementation *inside* an island core, on a three-rung ladder. Never exported, so a view cannot type against it. |
50:| **Rung** | 1 — descriptor re-exports (the CRUD default); 2 — island store (`@xstate/store`); 3 — statechart (XState) derived from a `core/domain` transition table. |
51:| **Graduation trigger** | The measurable condition that licenses moving up a rung: state survives component unmount, multi-component coordination inside the island, optimistic writes spanning more than one entity, undo/redo, validation with dependencies. Enumerable states with transition-legality rules trigger rung 3. A graduating PR must name its trigger. |
52:| **Descriptors** | The typed query/mutation definitions produced by `core/client` factories (`defineQuery`, `defineMutation`) and bound once in `api.ts`. The descriptor object is the server-state seam. |
53:| **Bound action** | A descriptor after `api.ts` has bound it to its transport. Features import these; they never see an `ApiClient`, a port or an adapter. |
54:| **Bus** | Typed, closed unions of client-only, **ephemeral** signals **between island cores**; views never see it. Decided in ADR-0005; the module lands with the first bus event. |
55:| **Transition table** | The plain-data source of truth for guarded transitions, in `core/domain` — guard ids per destination column. Both the server check and the island's statechart are derived from it. |
56:| **Oracle** | The table-derived domain machine, consulted by the island's own UI machine (as a guard call, or as an invoked child actor) and never containing UI states. Direction is one-way: UI machine → derived domain machine. |
57:| **Drift test** | The CI property test that sweeps enumerated states across both derivations of the transition table, proves non-vacuity, and proves its own detection power with a planted mutant. |
61:## Identity and authorization
63:| Term | Meaning |
64:|---|---|
65:| **Tenant** | A foundation entity (`tenants`), never a provider object. One instance hosts many tenants over one shared account pool — a creator's unrelated brands should be tenants, not new deployments. |
66:| **Instance** | One deployment with one database. New instances are for hard isolation only. |
67:| **Staff** | The `tenant_admins` aggregate: flat `owner` / `admin` grants. Deliberately no teams or organizations concept — multiple admins are just multiple rows. |
68:| **Member** | An end customer: a tenant-scoped aggregate of our own (profile, tags, GDPR consents, owned email snapshot, export). Not a provider object either. |
69:| **Principal** | What an identity *acts as* for a decision, derived not stored: `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `visitor`. |
70:| **Visitor** | An **authenticated** identity with neither a staff grant nor a membership — the tenant-less caller. Not the same as an unauthenticated public reader, which has no identity at all. |
71:| **Capability** | One entry per aggregate action in a closed union — `todo:read`, `staff:grant`, `domain:write`, … Named by the use-case, resolved by `decide(identity, capability)`. |
72:| **Grant table** | `Record<Capability, readonly Principal[]>` — the whole policy as data. **Default-deny**: a principal absent from a capability's list is denied, and there is no wildcard-allow. |
73:| **Tenant resolution** | Answering *which* tenant a request is for, in one fixed order: exact custom domain → subdomain label of `APP_BASE_DOMAIN` → `X-Tenant` header. Separate from authorization. |
74:| **Existence-hiding** | Returning `tenant_not_found` — byte-identical for "no such tenant" and "no access" — when a tenant was addressed by slug or header. Deliberate, and recorded so nobody "fixes" it to `forbidden`. |
75:| **Slug (value object)** | Free input is **normalized** (lowercased, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to single hyphens, ends trimmed) and then **validated** (3–63 chars, canonical pattern, not a reserved subdomain), so only one canonical form is ever persisted or resolved. |
80:## Errors and the contract
82:| Term | Meaning |
83:|---|---|
84:| **`Result<T, E>`** | `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error }`. Use-cases return it for domain errors instead of throwing. |
85:| **`AppError`** | `code` from the closed `ErrorCode` union, a `message`, and optional `details` (typically a zod `flatten()`). |
86:| **Error taxonomy** | The closed `ErrorCode` union, mapped exhaustively to HTTP statuses **and** to CLI exit codes in `core/contract/http-status.ts`. |
87:| **Envelope** | The single response shape: `{ ok: true, data }` or `{ ok: false, error }`, JSON on every path including 404 and 503. |
88:| **Normalization edge** | `app.onError` — the one place a thrown port promise becomes `internal`. Use-cases never grow per-call `try`/`catch` for infrastructure failures. |
89:| **Expand → contract** | The two-deploy discipline for any breaking change: deploy 1 adds the new shape alongside the old (both accepted and emitted), deploy 2 removes the old once every consumer moved. Used for both contract changes and destructive migrations — one vocabulary for both. |
90:| **Stale tab** | The only real client/server skew: a long-lived SPA session running yesterday's bundle. `core/client` zod-parses every response and fails loud rather than rendering wrong data. |
94:## Data
96:| Term | Meaning |
97:|---|---|
98:| **MUST-ATOMIC** | An operation that must never be observable half-done. Implemented as **one** port method backed by a sanctioned idiom, so the compiler prevents a caller from half-doing it. The list is machine-checked against `ports.ts`. |
99:| **Sanctioned idiom** | A single-statement CTE via `db.execute`, or `db.batch([...])`. Both are atomic on `node-postgres` **and** `neon-http`. |
100:| **The `neon-http` trap** | Interactive `db.transaction(async tx => …)` is atomic on `node-postgres` but **not** on Neon's stateless HTTP driver, so it is forbidden for any MUST-ATOMIC operation. |
101:| **Hard delete** | The default: a tenant-scoped delete removes the row. `deleted_at` is per-feature and rare, because "soft-delete everything" fails the first time a query forgets the filter. |
102:| **Tenant offboarding** | One `DELETE FROM tenants WHERE id = $1`: every tenant-scoped table FK-chains to `tenants(id)` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so the *database* guarantees no orphans. Shared account tables are deliberately outside the chain. |
103:| **Grandfather list** | The named set of existing tables that keep their legacy shape (text ids, text ISO timestamps) rather than being migrated. Documented legacy, never a template — and the list is **closed**. |
104:| **Invariant placement** | The deliberate choice of where a data invariant is enforced: at the DB, at the DB *and* the app boundary, or app-only with a stated reason the DB cannot express it. Default is push it to the DB. |
105:| **Backfill** | A resumable, idempotent batch data operation with a durable checkpoint (`backfill_checkpoints`), driven per target: a network-isolated internal endpoint on self-host, a secret-gated route on Vercel. |
109:## Gates, verification and doctrine
111:| Term | Meaning |
112:|---|---|
113:| **Gate** | A red-or-green mechanical check. The static gate is `npm run check`; the runtime gate is `npm run smoke`. Static-green is not done — the app must actually run. |
114:| **`check`** | `typecheck` + `typecheck:islands` + `lint` + `lock-lint` + `depcruise` + `knip` + `doc-lint` + `test:coverage`. |
115:| **`smoke`** | Boots the real server against a real database and drives health → sign-in → todos through the CLI, asserting taxonomy exit codes. `smoke:remote` runs the same CLI suite against a deployment URL. |
116:| **Attestation** | The release `version` + commit `sha` carried by every health response, so a smoke run can prove *which* deploy it verified. `sha` is a vendor-neutral `APP_COMMIT_SHA`; unset (local dev) it reports `unknown`. |
117:| **`EXPECTED_SHA`** | The deployment event's SHA, passed to `smoke:remote`, which asserts `health.sha === EXPECTED_SHA` — closing the "smoked the wrong deployment" class of failure. |
118:| **Canary tenant** | The ring-fenced smoke account and tenant that `smoke:remote` drives against live production. Disposable, belongs to no creator, and non-self-poisoning by construction: every card a run creates ends in an unbounded column. |
119:| **Config-regression probe** | A test whose subject is the **configuration**, not the code: it plants a violating fixture (or parses a doc block) and asserts the gate still fires. Lives in `config-regression/`. It is how a lint rule or a doc promise is kept from rotting. |
120:| **`doc-lint`** | The gate that keeps docs and enforcers in sync: removing an enforcer from config without updating the docs that promise it fails the build. It also lints the drizzle migration sequence. |
121:| **Enforcement matrix** | The four tiers every rule in the normative docs declares — **TYPE / LINT / TEST / REVIEW+AI** — each cell saying *how*, or `n/a` with a reason. A rule without a matrix is prose, and prose decays. |
122:| **NORMATIVE NOW** | A rule that applies to the current tree. |
123:| **NORMATIVE WHEN TRIGGERED** | A decided rule that activates on a **named** trigger, and is honestly not built until then. |
124:| **OUT OF SCOPE** | Deliberately not the foundation's problem, with the reason stated. |
125:| **Deferred-work register** | [`docs/backlog.md`](https://github.com/chomamateusz/agentproofarch/blob/main/docs/backlog.md) — accepted-but-unbuilt work and accepted verification residuals, each with a named trigger, so the architecture doc never carries a silent gap. |
126:| **Wide event** | One context-rich event per request per service hop: annotate the active span as context accrues, emit once. Never step-log. Observability, **not** an audit trail. |
127:| **TIMELINE-TRACE** | The security doctrine that every security claim must be justified by tracing the **actual** event order — who acts, when, with what privilege — not the intended order. A claim not walked step by step is a hypothesis, not a control. |
128:| **CHEAP SECRETS** | The doctrine that every production secret must be least-privilege, revocable, and asymmetric-verify where possible — because a production build sees them all. |
133:## Foundation lifecycle
135:| Term | Meaning |
136:|---|---|
137:| **The portable artifact** | The **enforcement configuration**, not the code: `eslint.config.js` + `eslint-plugin-agentproofarch/`, `.dependency-cruiser.cjs`, `tsconfig` strictness, the gate scripts, `config-regression/` and the CI workflows. It travels unchanged because it encodes the architecture structurally instead of describing it. |
138:| **`FOUNDATION.md`** | The provenance file a consuming app writes at its root: upstream repo URL, forked commit SHA, fork date, and the foundation-owned paths — so a foundation update is a mechanical diff over those paths, never a guess. |
139:| **Off the foundation** | Weakening a *structural* rule (a client importing `core/server`, a framework in `core/**`, dissolving the `core/contract` seam, throwing across a boundary, re-enabling `any`/`as`). A legitimate choice that forfeits the name and the guarantee — and `doc-lint` makes sure it cannot happen silently. |

229:## Troubleshooting
231:| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
232:|---|---|---|
233:| Every page fails with "response does not match the contract" | `dist/web` is a stale build and `dev:server` is serving it | `npm run build:web`, or use `dev:web` |
234:| `check` fails in `lock-lint` after adding a dependency | a bare `npm install` under npm 11 pruned optional entries | reinstall with `npx -y npm@10 install <pkg>` and commit the regenerated lockfile |
235:| `smoke` fails with "Dependencies are not installed" or a lockfile-drift list | `node_modules` does not match `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
236:| Signing in on `acme.localhost` does not carry over to `globex.localhost` | browsers reject `Domain=.localhost` cookies | expected in dev — sign in per subdomain |
237:| Sign-in returns 403 "invalid origin" | Better Auth requires the request `Origin` to match `APP_BASE_URL`; changing the port without changing `APP_BASE_URL` breaks it | keep `APP_PORT` and `APP_BASE_URL` in step |
238:| `db:migrate` / `db:seed` cannot connect | the Docker stack is not up, or Postgres is still starting | `npm run db:up`, then wait for its healthcheck |
239:| A magic-link command "sent" a mail you cannot find | there is no dev mail transport — Mailpit captured it | open `http://localhost:47980` |
240:| e2e fails at startup with the port already in use | a previous harness left the port bound | the harness now frees the port before boot ([#55](https://github.com/chomamateusz/agentproofarch/pull/55)); if it recurs, that is a P1 to file, not a job to rerun |

7:# Authorization (default-deny)
9:This page exists because "we check permissions in the handlers" is how
10:cross-tenant data leaks happen. Authorization here is **one pure function over
14:call. Nothing is granted by wildcard: a principal absent from a capability's list
15:is denied.
17:## Two questions, two steps
21:*what* they may do there. Keeping them separate is what makes the second step a
27:    pr --> owner["owner — staffRole is owner"]
28:    pr --> admin["admin — staffRole is admin"]
42:## The capability model
45:database, no I/O. The `Capability` union is closed:
60:The principal is derived, never stored:
71:`owner` and `admin` are **distinct principals**. They were a single `staff`
72:principal until FR-8; the staff-grant surface is the first capability where they
73:diverge, so the split is honest rather than cosmetic.
75:## The grant table
77:The policy is data — a `Record<Capability, readonly Principal[]>` — so adding a
80:| capability | owner | admin | member | visitor (tenant-less) |
81:|---|---|---|---|---|
82:| `todo:read` | allow | allow | allow | deny |
83:| `todo:write` | allow | allow | allow | deny |
84:| `card:read` | allow | allow | allow | deny |
85:| `card:write` | allow | allow | allow | deny |
86:| `member:read` | allow | allow | deny | deny |
87:| `member:write` | allow | allow | deny | deny |
88:| `member:remove` | allow | allow | deny | deny |
89:| `member:export` | allow | allow | deny | deny |
90:| `staff:read` | allow | allow | deny | deny |
91:| `staff:grant` | allow | **deny** | deny | deny |
92:| `staff:revoke` | allow | **deny** | deny | deny |
93:| `domain:read` | allow | allow | deny | deny |
94:| `domain:write` | allow | **deny** | deny | deny |
95:| `tenant:create` | allow | allow | **deny** | **allow** |
99:- **Members are full collaborators, not administrators.** `todo:*` and `card:*`
100:  are granted to `member` because todos and cards are collaborative aggregates.
101:  Tenant administration is not.
102:- **`member:*` is staff-only on purpose.** Members are the end customers this
103:  aggregate is *about*, managed **by** staff — granting a member `member:read`
105:  legitimate self-scoped read is `/api/me`, which carries no capability.
106:  `member:remove` is split from `member:write` so a future policy can reserve
108:- **Only an owner may mint or remove staff** (FR-8). An admin runs the tenant but
110:  that returns a `validation` error from `revokeAdmin`. Granting admin targets an
111:  **existing** account by email (there are no invitations yet), so `grantAdmin`
112:  returns `not_found` when the email has no account.
113:- **`domain:write` is owner-only** for the same reason: an admin runs the tenant
114:  without changing *where it is reachable*.
115:- **`tenant:create` is tenant-less self-service** — the caller becomes owner — so a

167:## Public routes never authorize
169:The public contract group (`/api/public/*`) is unauthenticated, so expressing its
170:reads as a `visitor` capability would be dishonest — `visitor` is an
171:*authenticated* tenant-less principal, and a public reader is not authenticated at
172:all ([ADR-0006](../decisions/0006-public-read-only-surface.md)).
174:Instead the public handlers are registered **ahead of** the `/api/*`
175:tenant-resolution middleware and call only use-cases that take **no** identity
180:That is enforced, not asserted: `config-regression/public-surface.test.ts` scans
183:parameter is not `ctx: Ctx`.
185:## How each rule is actually held
187:The foundation's convention is that every rule carries an explicit enforcement
188:matrix, because a rule without one is prose, and prose decays.
190:| Tier | What it holds here |
191:|---|---|
192:| **TYPE** | `Capability` is a closed union and the helpers take it as a required argument, so a use-case cannot name a capability the union does not declare. `Record<Capability, readonly Principal[]>` is exhaustive, so adding a capability without deciding its grants fails to compile. |
193:| **LINT** | *n/a* — "call the predicate first" is a call-site discipline, not a syntactic shape a rule can match. |
194:| **TEST** | the exhaustive `decide` matrix, per-use-case denial tests, the scaffolder's generated tests, and the structural probe (below). |
195:| **REVIEW+AI** | flag a tenant-scoped use-case that touches a repository *before* the predicate, any grant that widens a capability beyond the table above, and any new entry in the probe's authentication-only allowlist without a self-scoped-read rationale. |
197::::caution Honest limit of the type tier
199:never calls `authorize`/`authorizeTenant` at all still typechecks. That gap is why
200:the structural probe below exists — and why the probe's own limits are stated
202::::
204:## The denial tests
209:the table above is pinned. It also asserts the structural properties: a denial
210:always carries a reason and a grant never does, `owner` holds every capability,
211:and `admin` is denied exactly the owner-only rows (the FR-8 split).
220:guidance for a staff-only aggregate), and the tenant-less caller `forbidden`. A

231:- an intentional authentication-only use-case is a **named, reasoned allowlist

7:# Client state (island cores)
9:This page exists because client state is where architectures usually stop being
10:architecture. The rules here are unusual in one specific way: **the seam a view
11:talks to is identical on every rung of complexity**, so upgrading a feature from
12:"no client state" to "a full statechart" is a change *inside* the island and
14:sure they cannot find out. The model is decided in
17:## Feature, island, core — three words for one thing
19:| Word | Meaning |
20:|---|---|
21:| **Feature** | `apps/web/src/features/<name>/` — the vertical slice of a business subdomain in the UI |
22:| **Island** | the same feature, named after its isolation guarantee: lint forbids features to import each other |
23:| **Island core** | `features/<name>/core/` — a pure TS module: events in, selectors out, machine inside |
24:| **View** | a React component inside the feature; talks exclusively to its own island's core |
26:A business **subdomain** is not a feature: the demo has one tasks subdomain and
28:distinction is the whole reason `core/domain` is singular while `features/` is
31:## The seam: events in, selectors out
33:Every island core's public API is a closed event union plus selector functions.
34:The machine is **not exported**, so a view cannot type against it:
44:`send` returns `void`. That is the CQRS partition applied recursively at the
45:view↔core seam: **events are writes, selectors are reads, and an event never
46:returns data.** Request/response over events is what kills this pattern, and the
47:return type makes it unwritable — there is nothing to await and nothing to
50:The web adapter is one line of glue: feed `subscribe` plus the `snapshot` selector
54:## Portable by construction
56:An island core is a **factory over its dependencies**, not a module that reaches
65:Composition moves **out** of the core. `features/<name>/index.web.ts` is the one
82:`useQuery`/invalidation at the view but never looks inside them, so it needs no
84:`api.ts`, but `api.ts` must never import a feature, which is why the transport is
88:| Portability property | How it is guaranteed |
89:|---|---|
90:| the core imports no `api.ts` and no web composition | `no-restricted-imports` parent-relative ban + depcruise `island-core-is-portable` + a config-regression probe |
91:| the core typechecks without a DOM | `tsconfig.islands.json` (`lib: ["ES2023"]`, **no DOM**) run as `typecheck:islands` inside `check` |
92:| the public seam runs in plain node | a per-island node test driving `createXCore(deps)` with a fake gateway — no jsdom |
93:| composition happens at exactly one site | `features/<name>/index.web.ts`; `api.ts` stays feature-free |
95:So "DOM-free" is proven by a compiler program, not asserted in prose: a core that
98:## The three-rung ladder
100:The seam is uniform; the **machine** escalates.
113:| Rung | Machine | Demo exemplar |
114:|---|---|---|
115:| 1 | none — the core re-exports the feature's bound descriptors; `send` is a typed, exhaustive stub | `features/members/core/` |

370:## Server state stays separate
372:Server state is TanStack Query only, consuming **bound actions**: `core/client`
374:features import ready actions. Feature code never holds an `ApiClient`, a port or
375:an adapter, never defines `queryKey`/`queryFn` inline, and never touches `fetch` —
376:all lint. The **descriptor object is the seam**, and TanStack is a vocabulary
377:dependency, never wrapped in a port.
379:The CQRS partition is type-enforced end to end: contract route methods carry a
380:phantom read/write brand through `core/client`, so `defineQuery` accepts only a
381:`GET`-tagged call and `defineMutation` only a write-tagged one. Every client — web,
384:URL state has its own rule: **path params are resource identity, search params are
385:shareable filters**, and neither is duplicated into component state.
387:## Other apps/web rules worth knowing
389:- `main.tsx` is composition only: providers plus router wiring.
390:- `routes/` are thin: parse params, render a feature. No core, no adapters, no api
392:- `components/ui/` is presentational: no core, no features, no TanStack.
393:- `lib/` is pure TypeScript with no React and no app-internal imports.
394:- `theme.ts` is the entire visual language — no colors or fonts anywhere else, held
395:  by `agentproofarch/sx-layout-only` above rather than by convention.
396:- Non-trivial behaviour extracts to `*.logic.ts` and is unit-tested without
397:  rendering; component tests use real providers plus MSW, **never hook mocks**.
399:  context is for cross-cutting concerns only (theme, session).
401::::caution Two app-level policies are prescribed but not wired
403:splitting) is prescribed, thresholds are per app, and **no size gate is wired
404:yet**. **Browser matrix** — the intended default is evergreen-latest only

20:Two drivers are selected by `DB_DRIVER` (`node-postgres` for self-host and dev,
24:| Idiom | `node-postgres` (self-host / dev) | `neon-http` (Vercel) |
25:|---|---|---|
26:| single-statement CTE, one `db.execute` | atomic — one statement is always its own transaction | **atomic** — one HTTP request is one implicit transaction |
27:| `db.batch([...])` | atomic — wrapped in one `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` | **atomic** — Neon runs the array in one HTTP request/transaction |
28:| interactive `db.transaction(async tx => …)` | atomic — real `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` on one pooled connection | **NOT atomic** — the HTTP driver is stateless; each `tx` query is a separate request, so a mid-sequence failure leaves earlier writes committed |

113:unique index (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`) is mandatory wherever a soft-deleted row

116:posture is to keep the soft-deleting surface tiny. **No current aggregate uses
119:**Tenant offboarding is a schema invariant** (normative now). Every tenant-scoped
120:table FK-chains to `tenants(id)` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so offboarding is one
134:`deleteTenant` therefore issues no child deletes at all. Global/shared tables are
135:outside the chain on purpose: one account spans many tenants, so it must never
136:cascade from a single tenant's deletion. The invariant is mechanically checkable —
138:rows remain — and that pattern is normative with the demo implementing on first

168:## Data conventions
171:shape. Existing tables are grandfathered where noted: documented legacy, never a
174:| Convention | Status | Rule |
175:|---|---|---|
176:| **Money** | normative now, **not yet exercised** | integer minor units plus a closed ISO-4217 currency union — `amountMinor` + `currency`, defined once in `core/domain` when the first money aggregate lands. Never floats, never `numeric`/`real`/`double` columns |
177:| **Timestamps** | normative now for **new** tables | `timestamp('…', { withTimezone: true })`; the domain and contract keep speaking ISO-8601 strings, with the mapping at the adapter's column |
178:| **IDs** | normative now for **new** tables | native `uuid('id')` primary keys, application-minted; an FK column always matches the type of the key it references |
179:| **List pagination** | normative now for **future** list endpoints | cursor-based: request `?cursor=<opaque>&limit=<n>` with a server-side cap; response `{ items, nextCursor }` where `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page. Never a raw offset |
180:| **Concurrency** | normative now | last-write-wins, **documented per aggregate**. The named upgrade is a `version` column with `WHERE version = $expected`, adopted per aggregate when its trigger fires |
185:reintroduces binary floats, JSON has no decimal type), while integer minor units
186:are exact in every layer, sum and compare with plain integer arithmetic, and are
188:(micro-units); formatting for humans is a view concern (`Intl.NumberFormat`), never
193:is stable and index-backed.

200:| generated Better Auth tables | naive `timestamp`, non-UUID ids | **No** — provider-owned |

217:## Invariant placement matrix
219:Every data invariant is placed deliberately — at the database, at the database
220:*and* the app boundary, or app-only with a stated reason why the DB cannot express
221:it — and each placement carries its test. The default is **push it to the DB**: a
225:| Invariant | Enforced where | Mechanism and test |
226:|---|---|---|
227:| `tenant_admins.role` in `('owner','admin')` | **DB + app** | DB `CHECK` `tenant_admins_role_check` (migration `0006`); the adapter also zod-parses on read. Test: raw-SQL bad role is rejected |
228:| `tenant_domains.kind` in `('subdomain','custom')` | **DB** | `CHECK` `tenant_domains_kind_check`. Test: raw-SQL bad kind rejected |
229:| `cards.board` in `('personal','team')` | **DB + app** | `CHECK` `cards_board_check`; use-cases validate at their boundary. Test: raw-SQL bad board rejected |
230:| `cards.column` legal for its `board` | **DB + app** | compound `CHECK` `cards_column_check` over `(board, column)` pairs; each board validates its column at the use-case. Test: raw-SQL `personal`/`in-dev` rejected |
231:| `members.marketing_consents[].channel` in `MarketingChannel` | **app-only** (zod at the read boundary) | jsonb — a per-element closed set no column `CHECK` can express — so `memberSchema.parse` at the repository boundary **throws** rather than leaking an untyped channel into core. Test: raw-SQL garbage channel makes `findMember` throw |
232:| `cards` row shape (int position ≥ 0, board enum, string array `visited`) | **app-only** (zod at the read boundary) | `cardSchema.parse` on read throws on a corrupted row. Test: raw-SQL negative position makes `listByTenant` throw |
233:| a tenant always has ≥ 1 owner | **app**, one atomic conditional statement | a cross-row cardinality invariant Postgres cannot express as a column constraint → `revokeLastOwnerSafe` under a row lock. Test: two concurrent revokes, tenant never reaches zero owners |
234:| every tenant-scoped row cascades from `tenants(id)` | **DB** (FK `ON DELETE CASCADE`) | the offboarding-cascade integration test |

17:## Who are you, versus who are you here
21:- **Global account = authentication only.** One account per email, holding
23:  Auth is the default adapter; its topology (embedded, separate container, SaaS)
24:  is a composition-root choice.
26:  There is deliberately **no teams/organizations concept**; multiple admins are
31:No auth-provider organization/team feature is used for either population. The
35:creation must never depend on the auth provider.
37:`userId` is an **opaque string**. Foundation tables never FK provider tables.
39:## The tables and their cascade posture
60:| Table | Owns | Key columns | Cascade |
61:|---|---|---|---|
62:| `tenants` | the tenant itself | `id` (text), `slug` (unique), `name`, `created_at` | root of the chain |
63:| `tenant_admins` | staff grants | `tenant_id` FK, `user_id` (opaque), `role` | `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `tenants`; unique on `(tenant_id, user_id)` |
64:| `members` | the customer relationship | `tenant_id` FK, nullable `user_id`, `email`, `tags`, `marketing_consents`, `external_customer_ids` | `ON DELETE CASCADE`; unique on `(tenant_id, user_id)` and `(tenant_id, email)` |
65:| `tenant_domains` | where the tenant is reachable | `tenant_id` FK, `domain` (globally unique), `kind` (`subdomain`/`custom`), `verified` | `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
66:| provider tables | credentials, sessions, 2FA secrets, passkeys | provider-generated ids | **deliberately outside the chain** — one account spans many tenants |
70:- **Tenant offboarding is one statement.** `DELETE FROM tenants WHERE id = $1`

160:## Tenant addressing per environment
162:This is the honest table. "Base domain" means something different in each
165:| Environment | Tenant addressing | Session scope | Caveat |
166:|---|---|---|---|
167:| **Local dev** (`*.localhost`) | full subdomain tenancy — `acme.localhost:47100` | **per-subdomain** | browsers reject `Domain=.localhost` cookies, so a session does not span siblings; `crossSubDomainCookies` is off for `localhost` |
168:| **Vercel shared apex** (`<project>.vercel.app`) | **impossible** — see below | single deployment URL | `tenantUrl()` returns `null`; web runs single-tenant, multi-tenancy is CLI-only via `X-Tenant` |
169:| **Real base domain + wildcard** (`*.example.com`) | full subdomain tenancy, one wildcard resolves all tenants | spans sibling subdomains (`crossSubDomainCookies` on) | wildcard cert needs an ACME **DNS-01** challenge → NS delegation to Vercel (or `_acme-challenge` delegation) |
170:| **Custom domain** (`shop.acme.com`) | step 1 of resolution, once `verified` | **its own cookie world** — sign-in per domain, deliberate isolation | Vercel attaches each host through the US-020 Domains API adapter (built, `VERCEL_TOKEN` pending); self-host needs nothing |
171:| **Docker self-host** | subdomain *and* custom domain both work | as configured | Caddy `on_demand_tls` asks an internal endpoint before minting a cert |

175:This is a platform restriction, confirmed live — not a configuration mistake:
177:> `<team>` does not have access to `*.<project>.vercel.app` domains
194:web app is single-tenant per deployment URL while the API and CLI stay fully

198:### The custom-domain path
200:The way out is a real owned base domain, or per-tenant custom domains:
202:| Concern | Vercel target | Docker self-host |
203:|---|---|---|
204:| Wildcard cert | ACME DNS-01 → **NS delegation** to Vercel, or narrow `_acme-challenge` delegation | Caddy on-demand TLS, no wildcard needed |
205:| Records-only DNS (no NS delegation) | individual non-wildcard per-tenant hosts (HTTP-01 via CNAME), each attached to the project by the US-020 adapter | n/a |
206:| Domain provisioning port | `vercel` adapter (**built**, US-020): `provision`/`remove` attach and detach the host over the Domains API, `check` reads the domain and its config back — live run pending `VERCEL_TOKEN` | `caddy` adapter (**built**): `provision`/`remove` are no-ops, `check` is a DNS lookup against `SELF_HOST_TARGET_CNAME`/`_IP` |
207:| Plan limits | Hobby caps at **50 custom domains per project**; a wildcard is not itself Pro-gated (Pro is a ToS/commercial requirement) | none |

152:## What knip enforces
154:`npm run knip` is the dead-weight gate — the reason a generated file that nothing
155:imports cannot quietly accumulate. Its rule severities are a deliberate split
158:| knip rule | Severity | Meaning |
159:|---|---|---|
160:| `files` | **error** | a source file nothing reaches is dead — delete it |
161:| `dependencies` / `unlisted` | **error** | an unused `package.json` entry, or an import with no declared dependency |
162:| `unresolved` | **error** | an import that resolves to nothing |
163:| `binaries` | **error** | a script calling a binary no dependency provides |
164:| `duplicates` | **error** | the same export exposed twice |
165:| `exports` / `types` / `nsExports` / `nsTypes` / `enumMembers` | **warn** | reported, does **not** fail `check` |
167::::caution Honest caveat: unused *exports* are warnings, not errors
168:`exports` and `types` are `warn` on purpose. The foundation ships API surface
172:tighten them to `error` once that scope is built — until then, "no unused export"
173:is *not* a guarantee this repo makes.
174::::

179:(codegen config, never imported), `scripts/*`, the Playwright specs under `e2e/`

7:# Ports & adapters
9:This page exists to answer two questions precisely: **what is actually behind a
10:port in this repo today**, and **when are you allowed to add one**. The second
11:question matters more than it looks — a port with exactly one implementation
12:forever is not architecture, it is a second copy of a library's API. So the rule
13:is blunt: *add a port only when a second implementation or a platform difference
14:actually exists*, and everything below is either a port that clears that bar or an
17:## How a port works here
19:A port is a plain TypeScript `interface` in `core/server` (or, for the one client
34:  `Result<T, AppError>`; a rejected port promise is an infrastructure failure,
39:- **Ports are called from use-cases only** — never from a route, never from another

135:### `DomainPort` per target
137:| Provisioner | Target | `provision` / `remove` | `check` |
138:|---|---|---|---|
139:| `vercel` | the Vercel target | attach / detach the host on the Vercel project over the Domains API | the project's domain + config endpoints report `verified` and not `misconfigured` |
140:| `caddy` | Docker self-host | no-ops — Caddy issues certificates on demand | DNS lookup that the domain resolves to `SELF_HOST_TARGET_CNAME` or `SELF_HOST_TARGET_IP` |
141:| `noop` (default) | dev | no-ops | always accepts |
144:ACME DNS-01 challenge, hence NS delegation. Where the base domain is a company
146:but certs are **per host over HTTP-01**, so each host must be attached to the
147:project individually — which is exactly what `provision` does. Attach is
148:convergent: an already-attached host (`409`) is a success, so the use-case may
149:retry. The token travels only in the `Authorization` header, never into a log or
150:an error detail, and every API response is zod-parsed at the boundary.
152::::caution `vercel` is proven against a stubbed `fetch` only
153:The adapter has **never run against the live Domains API** — CI and the build
156:nothing more. The owner supplying the token is what closes the gap; the first real
157:add/check/remove is the acceptance run.

168:## The composition root

171:Platform names may appear here and in adapters, never in core.

216:| Variable | Values | Default | Selects |

238:## Vendor containment
240:Every vendor SDK is fenced to the one directory that owns it — and the fences are
243:| Vendor | Allowed only in | Rule |
244:|---|---|---|
245:| `@vercel/*`, `@neondatabase/*` | `adapters/**`, plus the platform entry `api/index.ts` | `vercel-and-neon-only-in-adapters` |
246:| `better-auth`, `@better-auth/*` | `adapters/auth` | `auth-provider-sdk-only-in-adapters-auth` |
247:| `nodemailer`, `@aws-sdk/*` | `adapters/email` | `smtp-sdk-only-in-adapters-email` |
248:| `@sentry/node`, `@sentry/react` | the server's and web's composition-root sink modules | contained by convention — an error sink is **config, not a port** (a `SentryPort` would be port theater) |
250:## Deferred and not built
252:Stated plainly, because an aspirational port is worse than no port:
254:| Port | Status | Trigger |
255:|---|---|---|
256:| `StoragePort` | **not built** — shape, adapters and rules are fixed in the docs | the first feature that persists a caller-supplied binary (avatar, product asset, a GDPR-export file outliving one request). In-request bytes streamed straight to a response do **not** trigger it |
257:| `JobsPort` | **not built** — the platform difference is proven, the need is not | the first real deferred job. Executor would differ per target: a drain endpoint plus a QStash schedule on Vercel, a resident pg-boss worker on self-host |
259:`StoragePort`'s shape is already decided so the first implementation has nothing to
261:`remove(tenantId, path)`; **tenant scoping is the port's job** (the caller passes a
263:path that escapes the prefix, so the key space is closed by construction); and
264:**reads go through short-lived signed URLs** — objects are private, and the client
265:never receives a bucket credential or a permanent public URL.
267:## When to add a port
273:    second -->|yes| shape{"is it infrastructure, or vocabulary?"}
279::::danger Port theater
280:An interface with exactly one implementation forever re-states a library's API
282:would have to re-type `status`/`fetchStatus`, invalidation and optimistic-update
284:deliberately *not* built: an `IStore` interface over the island-store library (the
285:island core's own API is the facade), and a Sentry port (an error sink is config).
286::::
288:The corollary is the cheerful one: because the ports are few and small, swapping a
289:platform really is a composition-root edit. Both deploy targets run from the same

55:## Registration order in `app.ts`
57:Hono matches in registration order, so this list *is* the lifecycle. Everything
60:| # | Registered | Scope | What it does |
61:|---|---|---|---|
62:| 1 | `secureHeaders(...)` | `*` | CSP (`script-src 'self'`), `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` |
63:| 2 | `bodyLimit(...)` | `/api/*` | 100 KB cap; over-limit returns a `validation` **envelope**, never a non-JSON body |
64:| 3 | `telemetryMiddleware` | `*` | one wide span per request; continues an incoming `traceparent` |
65:| 4 | `app.onError` | — | the single normalization edge (see below) |
66:| 5 | `/api/health/live`, `/api/health/ready`, `/api/health` | exact | liveness never touches the DB; all three carry the build attestation |
67:| 6 | Better Auth handler | its own prefix | `GET`/`POST` delegated to `deps.auth.handler` |
68:| 7 | `/api/config` | exact | unauthenticated flags read by the pre-auth login page (`googleEnabled`) |
69:| 8 | `/api/internal/backfills/:name` | exact, **conditional** | mounted only when `INTERNAL_BACKFILL_SECRET` is set; gated by an `x-internal-secret` header |
70:| 9 | `registerPublicRoutes(app, deps)` | `/api/public/*` | open `GET` CORS + the two public tenant routes |
71:| 10 | `GET`/`POST` `/api/tenants` | exact | tenancy self-service — authenticated, deliberately *above* tenant resolution |
72:| 11 | **tenant middleware** | `/api/*` | authenticate → `resolveIdentity` → `c.set('identity', ...)` |
73:| 12 | `/api/me`, todos, cards, members, staff, domains | `/api/*` | tenant-scoped routes; every handler parses input with a contract schema |
74:| 13 | `app.all('/api/*', ...)` | `/api/*` | totalizer: taxonomy `not_found` envelope for an unmatched path or wrong method |
76::::note Why three surfaces sit above identity resolution
77:They are three different reasons, all deliberate:
79:- **Health** must answer when the database is unreachable — that is the whole
81:- **The public group** (`/api/public/*`) is unauthenticated by design. Because it
82:  is registered before the middleware, a public handler *structurally cannot*
84:  probe (`config-regression/public-surface.test.ts`) asserts exactly that.
85:- **`/api/tenants`** is self-scoped: listing and creating *your own* tenants must
86:  work on any host, including a tenant domain the caller has no access to (where
89::::
92:returns Hono's bare `text/plain` 404, which `core/client` can only degrade into a
94:taxonomy honest — and the Better Auth prefix is explicitly carved out so a real
95:auth route is never masked by our envelope.

     7	
     8	# agentproofarch
     9	
    10	When an AI agent writes most of the code, the thing that decays first is not
    11	correctness — it is *structure*. A generated change lands wherever it compiles,
    12	the seams blur, and six weeks later nobody can say where the boundary between the
    13	database and the domain went. **agentproofarch** is the answer to that specific
    14	failure: a strictly layered full-stack TypeScript foundation where every boundary
    15	is machine-enforced by lint, every capability is drivable from a CLI with `--json`
    16	output and deterministic exit codes, and "done" is defined as two green gates
    17	rather than a green typecheck. The architecture is written down first
    18	(`docs/architecture.md` is normative), the enforcers are written down next, and
    19	`demo/` is a running reference implementation of both.
    20	
    21	A free, open project by **Mateusz Choma**, developed privately in collaboration
    22	with **[CodeRoad.pl](https://coderoad.pl)** and
    23	**[AmazingDesign.eu](https://amazingdesign.eu)**.
    24	
    25	## What it is, precisely
    26	
    27	A pure-TypeScript core — `core/domain` (entities, `Result`, the error taxonomy),
    28	`core/contract` (routes + zod schemas), `core/server` (use-cases + ports),
    29	`core/client` (the typed HTTP client) — surrounded by thin adapters (Drizzle
    30	database, Better Auth, email, domain provisioning) and thin apps (a Hono HTTP
    31	server, a React SPA, a commander CLI). `core/**` may not import hono, react,
    32	drizzle, better-auth, pg or commander; `core/domain` depends on zod alone;
    33	`apps/server/src/composition.ts` is the only place a *server* adapter is
    34	instantiated. None of that is a convention you are asked to remember — it is
    35	`eslint-plugin-boundaries` plus dependency-cruiser, and violating it fails the
    36	build.
    37	
    38	The demo is a **walking skeleton**, not a scaffold: authentication (password,
    39	magic link, TOTP two-factor, passkeys, plus a Google seam that stays dormant
    40	unless both of its env vars are set), foundation-owned tenants with flat
    41	`owner`/`admin` staff grants, tenant resolution by custom domain or subdomain,
    42	end-customer members with GDPR export and removal, todos, two exemplar boards (a
    43	personal one and a WIP-guarded team one), and a public unauthenticated read
    44	surface — each one flowing through *every* layer and reachable from all three
    45	drive surfaces.
    46	
    47	## Who it is for
    48	
    49	| You are… | What you get from this |
    50	|---|---|
    51	| **Building a multi-tenant SaaS with agents doing the typing** | A layout where a generated change either lands inside a seam or turns a gate red — plus a scaffolder that plants a resource and hands you the 12-step wiring checklist. |
    52	| **Evaluating how far layering can actually be enforced** | A concrete answer: `eslint-plugin-boundaries`, dependency-cruiser, custom `agentproofarch/*` rules, a docs↔enforcer cross-check (`doc-lint`), and probes that feed each rule a violating fixture to prove it still bites. |
    53	| **Deciding whether to trust an AI-written codebase** | The verification story, warts included: a fail-closed AI-review gate, post-deploy commit-SHA attestation, a flake-is-a-P1 rule, and a register of work that was accepted and deliberately *not* built. |
    54	| **Planning to self-host** | The same commit runs on Vercel + Neon and on a Docker stack (Node + Postgres + Caddy on-demand TLS), with a CI job that boots the container stack and smokes it. |
    55	
    56	:::note This is a reference implementation, not a package
    57	`demo/package.json` is `private: true`, nothing is published to npm, and the
    58	project carries no version numbers — a release is a branch promotion
    59	(`main` → `production`). You read it, fork it, or lift patterns out of it. CLI
    60	distribution and a version handshake sit on the
    61	[deferred-work register](https://github.com/chomamateusz/agentproofarch/blob/main/docs/backlog.md)
    62	with "first external CLI consumer" as the named trigger.
    63	:::
    64	
    65	## The feature map
    66	
    67	Every capability is reachable three ways, and the CLI path is the one an agent
    68	uses — because it is the only one with machine-readable output and a
    69	taxonomy-mapped exit code.
    70

   115	
   116	Read the structure top-down in [Layers](../architecture/layers.md), then follow a
   117	single request through it in
   118	[Request lifecycle](../architecture/request-lifecycle.md).
   119	
   120	## Why — the four promises
   121	
   122	The architecture exists so four things stay true while agents do the work
   123	([architecture.md](https://github.com/chomamateusz/agentproofarch/blob/main/docs/architecture.md),
   124	"The promise"):
   125	
   126	1. **An agent works, and the architecture does not move.** Generated change lands
   127	   inside the seams; drift is a red gate, not a slow surprise.
   128	2. **The platform is replaceable without a rewrite.** Deploy target, database
   129	   driver and auth provider are adapter choices behind ports — a composition-root
   130	   edit, not a migration.
   131	3. **A feature enters and leaves touching nothing but its communication
   132	   interfaces.** Adding or removing a vertical slice changes that slice and its
   133	   declared seams, nothing else.
   134	4. **Everything is testable.** Cores are pure and test without frameworks; the
   135	   rest is driven end-to-end by the gates — static, runtime, browser.
   136	
   137	## How it defends itself
   138	
   139	| Gate | Command | What it proves | Required check? |
   140	|---|---|---|---|
   141	| **Static** | `npm run check` | typecheck (incl. the island TS project) + ESLint boundaries + `lock-lint` + dependency-cruiser + knip + `doc-lint` + vitest with a coverage ratchet | yes — `check` |
   142	| **Runtime** | `npm run smoke` | recreates an isolated database, boots the real server, drives health → sign-in → todos → unauthorized through the CLI asserting taxonomy exit codes | yes — `smoke` |
   143	| **Browser** | `npm run e2e` | a real Chromium over the real stack: 15 tests across 6 spec files | yes — `e2e` |
   144	| **Container** | `selfhost.yml` | builds the image, boots `docker-compose.prod.yml`, smokes the container through the CLI | yes — `docker-smoke` |
   145	| **Pixel** | `npm run visual` | Playwright `toHaveScreenshot()` against CI-rendered baselines ([ADR-0008](../decisions/0008-visual-regression.md)) | **no** — by design |
   146	| **Review** | `ai-review.yml` | fail-closed AI diff review; only a positive `PASS` verdict is green | **no** — until armed |
   147	
   148	:::danger Done = `check` green AND `smoke` green
   149	Static-green is not done. A typechecked, linted commit that does not boot is a
   150	red commit. And a red gate is never rerun to green: **a flake is a P1 bug**
   151	(owner ruling, DECIDE F3) — a red gate means the commit is wrong or the gate is
   152	wrong, and one of them gets fixed.
   153	:::
   154	
   155	Underneath those gates: **84** test files in the database-free run, **48**
   156	integration tests against a real Postgres, **15** Playwright tests, and **47**
   157	config-regression probes that feed a deliberately illegal fixture to an enforcer
   158	and assert it still rejects it — so a silently weakened rule fails CI instead of
   159	passing quietly. Those counts are injected into the repository's own READMEs by
   160	`doc-lint` and re-verified against the source tree on every `check`. See
   161	[Testing doctrine](../guides/testing-doctrine.md) and
   162	[CI gates](../operations/ci-gates.md).
   163	
   164	## Live demo
   165	
   166	[agentproofarch.vercel.app](https://agentproofarch.vercel.app) — sign in as
   167	`demo@agentproofarch.dev` / `demo1234`. The deployed web app is single-tenant on
   168	`*.vercel.app` (Vercel refuses tenant subdomains under a project's own
   169	`*.vercel.app` apex, so a wildcard base domain is an environment concern, not a
   170	code one — [ADR-0003](../decisions/0003-vercel-environments.md)); the API and CLI
   171	stay fully multi-tenant via the `X-Tenant` header.
   172	
   173	## Honest status
   174	
   175	- **Vercel target: live. Docker self-host: built** and proven on every PR and push
   176	  to `main` by the `docker-smoke` job — a multi-stage `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.prod.yml`
   177	  with an `edge`-profiled Caddy for on-demand TLS, and migrations run by the
   178	  container entrypoint.
   179	- **The Vercel Domains provisioning adapter (US-020) is built but has never run
   180	  against the live API.** Its behaviour is proven only against a stubbed `fetch`,
   181	  because neither CI nor the build machine holds a `VERCEL_TOKEN`. The owner
   182	  supplying that token is what closes the gap; the first real add/check/remove is
   183	  the acceptance run. Self-host needs no such adapter — Caddy issues per-tenant
   184	  TLS on demand.
   185	- **Three CI jobs run but block nothing.** The `main-gates` and
   186	  `production-protection` rulesets name `check`, `smoke`, `e2e` and
   187	  `docker-smoke` only, so `visual` (pixel), `ai-review` (AI diff review) and
   188	  `docs-build` (this site) report without gating until the owner arms them.
   189	  Adding a status check to a ruleset is Admin-only — which the agent account
   190	  deliberately is not.
   191	- **`ai-review` has one token slot provisioned.** `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_1` is
   192	  present; slots `_2` and `_3` are wired in the workflow and skip cleanly while
   193	  absent. The gate is fail-closed by construction: an infra failure on every
   194	  available slot is RED, never a silent pass.
   195	- **Accepted-but-deliberately-unbuilt work is written down**, each entry with a
   196	  named trigger, in the
   197	  [deferred-work register](https://github.com/chomamateusz/agentproofarch/blob/main/docs/backlog.md)
   198	  — day-2 operations, threat model, feature flags, forms doctrine, a11y, i18n,
   199	  per-tenant SSO. When a trigger fires the entry graduates into an ADR or an
   200	  implementation slice; it never gets built silently.
   201

     6	
     7	# Quickstart
     8	
     9	This page takes you from `git clone` to a green **runtime** gate — the point where
    10	the real server has booted, the CLI has driven a full multi-tenant flow through it,
    11	and you can trust what you are looking at. It is deliberately not a "hello world":
    12	the same five minutes that start the dev server also seed two tenants, a demo
    13	account and a local mail sink, because every one of those is something the gates
    14	and the walkthroughs assume exists. Every command below is copied from
    15	`demo/package.json` and the repository READMEs.
    16	
    17	## Prerequisites
    18	
    19	| Tool | Version | Why exactly this |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| **Node** | 22 (`.nvmrc` pins it) | `engines.node` is `22.x`; the CI runner is node 22. |
    22	| **npm** | `>=10 <11` | `packageManager` is `npm@10.9.2`, and `lock-lint` validates the lockfile under npm-10 semantics. npm 11 breaks it — see the warning below. |
    23	| **Docker** | any recent | `npm run db:up` starts Postgres 16 and Mailpit from `docker-compose.dev.yml`. |
    24	
    25	Everything runs from `demo/` — it has its own `package.json`. The repository root
    26	holds `docs/` (normative architecture + PRD) and `website/` (this site).
    27	
    28	## 1. Clone and install
    29	
    30	```bash
    31	git clone https://github.com/chomamateusz/agentproofarch.git
    32	cd agentproofarch/demo
    33	nvm use          # or Corepack — anything that lands you on Node 22 / npm 10
    34	npm ci
    35	```
    36	
    37	:::danger Never `npm install` here
    38	`lock-lint` (part of `npm run check`) validates `package-lock.json` under npm-10
    39	semantics — exactly what `npm ci` enforces on the node-22 CI runner. A local
    40	npm 11 `npm install` silently prunes optional entries npm 10 requires, which
    41	**broke CI twice**. Add dependencies with `npx -y npm@10 install <pkg>`, never a
    42	bare `npm install`.
    43	:::
    44	
    45	## 2. Environment: nothing to do (locally)
    46	
    47	There is no `.env` step for local development. Every key the server needs has a
    48	dev default in the single env schema (`core/server/config.ts`): `DATABASE_URL`
    49	defaults to
    50	`postgresql://agentproofarch:agentproofarch@localhost:47542/agentproofarch`,
    51	`DB_DRIVER` to `node-postgres` off Vercel, `APP_BASE_DOMAIN` to `localhost`,
    52	`PORT` to `47100`, and `SMTP_HOST`/`SMTP_PORT` to the dev Mailpit. The dev-only
    53	`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` default is *refused* the moment the process looks deployed
    54	(`VERCEL` set, or `SECURE_COOKIES=true`), so the shortcut cannot leak into a
    55	deployment.
    56	
    57	You want `.env.example` in two cases only:
    58	
    59	```bash
    60	cp .env.example .env     # for: Docker self-host, or overriding a dev default
    61	```
    62	
    63	`.env.example` documents **names only**, and it is also the file `doc-lint` checks
    64	the env schema against — a new env key missing from it fails `check`.
    65	
    66	## 3. Database, mail sink, seed
    67	
    68	```bash
    69	npm run db:up            # Postgres 16 on 47542 + Mailpit on 47925 (SMTP) / 47980 (UI)
    70	npm run db:migrate       # tsx adapters/db/migrate.ts — applies the drizzle migrations
    71	npm run db:seed          # idempotent; running it twice is a no-op
    72	```
    73	
    74	The seed is worth knowing by heart, because the walkthroughs and the e2e specs all
    75	reference it:
    76	
    77	| Seeded | Value |
    78	|---|---|
    79	| Account | `demo@agentproofarch.dev` / `demo1234` (name: *Demo User*) |
    80	| Tenant 1 | `acme` — *Acme Sp. z o.o.*, demo user is **owner**, domain `acme.localhost` |
    81	| Tenant 2 | `globex` — *Globex Corp*, demo user is **admin**, domain `globex.localhost` |
    82	| Members | `alice@example.com` (acme, tagged `vip`, `early-adopter`), `mag@example.com` (acme, provisioned with no account yet — binds on first magic-link sign-in), `bob@example.com` (globex) |
    83	| Todos | two in `acme`, one in `globex` |
    84	
    85	On success it prints:
    86	
    87	```text
    88	Seed applied:
    89	  user     demo@agentproofarch.dev / demo1234
    90	  tenants  http://acme.localhost:47100  http://globex.localhost:47100
    91	```
    92	
    93	Mailpit is not optional scenery: there is **no separate dev email transport**. Dev,
    94	CI and e2e all run the real SMTP adapter pointed at Mailpit, which captures sends
    95	instead of delivering them. Read a magic link from its UI at
    96	`http://localhost:47980` — there is no in-app dev route for it.
    97	
    98	## 4. Run it
    99	
   100	Two dev paths, and picking the wrong one is the most common first-run
   101	frustration:
   102	
   103	```bash
   104	npm run dev:web          # Vite + hot reload on 47180 — the canonical frontend path
   105	```
   106	
   107	```bash
   108	npm run build:web        # …or a prod-like page: build the SPA first,
   109	npm run dev:server       # then the API + built bundle on http://acme.localhost:47100
   110	```
   111	
   112	:::warning `dev:server` serves a gitignored build
   113	`dev:server` serves whatever `dist/web` currently holds. After a contract change a
   114	stale bundle fails **every** page with "response does not match the contract" (a
   115	real incident, 2026-07-12). The server warns at boot when `dist/web` is missing or
   116	older than the web/contract sources; on that warning either `npm run build:web` or
   117	switch to `dev:web`. **All frontend work goes through `dev:web`.**
   118	:::
   119	
   120	Open both tenants and watch the isolation — each has its own todos and its own
   121	accent colour:
   122	
   123	- `http://acme.localhost:47100`
   124	- `http://globex.localhost:47100`
   125	
   126	Browsers reject `Domain=.localhost` cookies, so in dev you sign in **per
   127	subdomain**. On a real base domain one session spans every tenant subdomain; the
   128	per-subdomain login is a localhost artefact, not the design.
   129	
   130	## 5. Say hello from the CLI
   131	
   132	The CLI is the reference client and the agent feedback loop. `--silent` keeps npm's
   133	own chatter off stdout, so `--json` really does emit one document:
   134	
   135	```bash
   136	npm run --silent cli -- --json health
   137	npm run --silent cli -- login --email demo@agentproofarch.dev --password demo1234
   138	npm run --silent cli -- whoami
   139	npm run --silent cli -- --tenant acme todo list
   140	```
   141	
   142	Human output of that flow against a fresh seed:
   143	
   144	```text
   145	status=ok db=up v0.1.0 sha=unknown
   146	signed in as demo@agentproofarch.dev
   147	demo@agentproofarch.dev @ Acme Sp. z o.o. (acme, staff: owner)
   148	- Wdrożyć walking skeleton na produkcję  (3f8a1c02)
   149	- Sprawdzić izolację danych między tenantami  (b17d94ee)
   150	```
   151	
   152	`v0.1.0` is `package.json`'s version (the single release-identity source) and
   153	`sha=unknown` is the honest local answer — `APP_COMMIT_SHA` is only set by a
   154	deploy, where `smoke:remote` asserts it equals the promoted commit. The trailing
   155	parenthesis on a todo is the first 8 characters of its row id; the seed uses
   156	`crypto.randomUUID()`, so yours will differ. Full tour:
   157	[CLI walkthrough](../guides/cli-walkthrough.md).
   158	
   159	## 6. Run the gates
   160	
   161	```bash
   162	npm run check            # static: typecheck ×2 + eslint + lock-lint + depcruise + knip + doc-lint + coverage
   163	npm run smoke            # runtime: isolated DB, real server, CLI flow — ~5s
   164	```
   165	
   166	`smoke` assumes `npm run db:up` is running. It does **not** touch your dev-seeded
   167	database: it drops and recreates `agentproofarch_smoke`, migrates and seeds that,
   168	boots `entry.node.ts` on an ephemeral port, and drives the flow. A green run prints
   169	these phases (the port is ephemeral and the elapsed time is measured, so both vary):
   170	
   171	```text
   172	smoke: checking lockfile drift...
   173	smoke: preparing isolated database...
   174	smoke: waiting for Mailpit...
   175	smoke: booting server on port <ephemeral>...
   176	smoke: driving the CLI...
   177	
   178	smoke: PASS (5.1s)
   179	```
   180	
   181	The browser gate needs Chromium and a built bundle, so it is a separate command
   182	(and a separate CI job) — run it for any `apps/web` change:
   183	
   184	```bash
   185	npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
   186	npm run build:web
   187	npm run e2e
   188	```
   189	
   190	:::danger Static-green is not done
   191	**Done = `check` green AND `smoke` green.** Do not weaken a lint rule to make
   192	either go green, and do not rerun a red job until it passes — a flake is a P1 bug
   193	([Testing doctrine](../guides/testing-doctrine.md)).
   194	:::
   195	
   196	## The whole first run, in order
   197	
   198	```mermaid
   199	flowchart TD
   200	  clone["git clone · cd demo"] --> install["npm ci<br/>never npm install"]
   201	  install --> up["npm run db:up<br/>Postgres 47542 + Mailpit 47925/47980"]
   202	  up --> migrate["npm run db:migrate"]
   203	  migrate --> seed["npm run db:seed<br/>demo user · acme + globex"]
   204	  seed --> choose{"What are you doing?"}
   205	  choose -->|"frontend work"| devweb["npm run dev:web<br/>Vite on 47180"]
   206	  choose -->|"prod-like page"| build["npm run build:web"]
   207	  build --> devserver["npm run dev:server<br/>API + SPA on 47100"]
   208	  choose -->|"verify a capability"| clihello["npm run --silent cli -- --json health"]
   209	  devweb --> gates
   210	  devserver --> gates
   211	  clihello --> gates
   212	  gates["npm run check<br/>npm run smoke"] --> done["Done = both green"]
   213	```
   214	
   215	## Ports
   216	
   217	Nothing binds a common port, on purpose — 3000, 5432, 8080 and friends are all
   218	avoided so the stack never collides with whatever else you are running.
   219	
   220	| Port | Service |
   221	|---|---|
   222	| 47100 | API + built SPA (`dev:server`; the `PORT` default) |
   223	| 47180 | Vite dev server (`dev:web`) |
   224	| 47542 | Postgres 16 (`docker-compose.dev.yml`; override with `DB_PORT`) |
   225	| 47925 | Mailpit SMTP (override with `MAILPIT_SMTP_PORT`) |
   226	| 47980 | Mailpit web UI + HTTP API (override with `MAILPIT_API_PORT`) |
   227	| 47101 | Self-host only: the internal domain-check control plane (`INTERNAL_PORT`, unset in dev) |
   228	
   229	## Troubleshooting
   230	
   231	| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
   232	|---|---|---|
   233	| Every page fails with "response does not match the contract" | `dist/web` is a stale build and `dev:server` is serving it | `npm run build:web`, or use `dev:web` |
   234	| `check` fails in `lock-lint` after adding a dependency | a bare `npm install` under npm 11 pruned optional entries | reinstall with `npx -y npm@10 install <pkg>` and commit the regenerated lockfile |
   235	| `smoke` fails with "Dependencies are not installed" or a lockfile-drift list | `node_modules` does not match `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
   236	| Signing in on `acme.localhost` does not carry over to `globex.localhost` | browsers reject `Domain=.localhost` cookies | expected in dev — sign in per subdomain |
   237	| Sign-in returns 403 "invalid origin" | Better Auth requires the request `Origin` to match `APP_BASE_URL`; changing the port without changing `APP_BASE_URL` breaks it | keep `APP_PORT` and `APP_BASE_URL` in step |
   238	| `db:migrate` / `db:seed` cannot connect | the Docker stack is not up, or Postgres is still starting | `npm run db:up`, then wait for its healthcheck |
   239	| A magic-link command "sent" a mail you cannot find | there is no dev mail transport — Mailpit captured it | open `http://localhost:47980` |
   240	| e2e fails at startup with the port already in use | a previous harness left the port bound | the harness now frees the port before boot ([#55](https://github.com/chomamateusz/agentproofarch/pull/55)); if it recurs, that is a P1 to file, not a job to rerun |
   241

    35	  // (Caddy's on-demand-TLS `ask` endpoint). Set exclusively in the compose
    36	  // stack, where it is reachable only on the container network and never

    39	  INTERNAL_PORT: z.coerce.number().int().positive().optional(),

    43	  DOMAIN_PROVISIONER: z.enum(['vercel', 'caddy', 'noop']).default('noop'),

    54	```
    55	
    56	:::danger Done = `check` green AND `smoke` green
    57	Static-green is not done; the app must actually run. And do not weaken a lint rule
    58	to make either gate green — that inverts the whole point of having one.
    59	:::
    60	
    61	## Four levels: where does my test go?
    62	
    63	| Level | Command | Environment | Count today | Where it runs |
    64	|---|---|---|---|---|
    65	| **unit** | `npm run test` (inside `check`) | node + jsdom, **no database** | 84 test files | every `check`, locally and in CI |
    66	| **integration** | `npm run test:integration` | real Postgres, opt-in via `VITEST_INTEGRATION=1` | 48 tests | the CI `smoke` job — the only one with a database |
    67	| **e2e** | `npm run e2e` | real Chromium over the real stack | 15 tests / 6 specs | the CI `e2e` job |
    68	| **smoke** | `npm run smoke` | real server, driven through the CLI | the runtime gate | locally + the CI `smoke` job |
    69	| **remote smoke** | `npm run smoke:remote` | a deployed URL | same suite | `post-deploy-smoke`, after every deploy |
    70	| **pixel** | `npm run visual` | Chromium + CI-rendered baselines | own suite | the `visual` job — **not required** |
    71	
    72	The unit run is split into vitest **projects**, and which one your file lands in is
    73	decided by its path:
    74	
    75	| Project | Includes | Environment | Why |
    76	|---|---|---|---|
    77	| `node` | `core/**`, `adapters/**`, `apps/cli/**`, `apps/server/**`, `scripts/**`, the ESLint plugin, **and** `apps/web/src/features/*/core/**` | node | island cores are pure TS, so their tests run without jsdom — that is how TUI portability gets exercised on every `check` |
    78	| `web` | the rest of `apps/web/**` | jsdom + msw + user-event | component tests; 15s timeout because parallel CI load pushes render/settle waits past the 5s default |
    79	| `config` | `config-regression/**` | node | probes that run the real linter |
    80	| `integration` | `**/*.integration.test.ts` | node + Postgres | added only when `VITEST_INTEGRATION=1` |
    81	
    82	The `node` project explicitly **excludes** `*.integration.test.ts`, so a
    83	database-dependent test can never leak into a database-free run and fail
    84	mysteriously in `check`.
    85	
    86	Pixel comparison lives in its own suite and its own config
    87	(`playwright.visual.config.ts`) so a moved screenshot can never redden `e2e`
    88	([ADR-0008](../decisions/0008-visual-regression.md)).
    89
